correctness.rationale: For each plane normal the five-edge section-offset interval equals the exact inclusion-exclusion tent function; integration with the conditioned Crofton measure reduces to an explicit arctangent integral. Nine-edge crossing integration yields the other two probabilities. Six transverse edge-projection collisions supply the thin inverse-side coefficient by an integrable rescaling, and uniform large-height expansion plus exact angular integration supplies the positive tall coefficient. These steps prove the asserted full quantifiers, and deterministic edge-enumeration tests independently support the formulas without being used as universal proof.

originality.rationale: Under presently accessible evidence, the arbitrary-scalene Crofton law and its reciprocal-side thin correction and angle-weighted tall coefficient are not implied by the inspected full texts on mean counts or attainable slices. The exact equilateral-base Crofton law is already present in the prior mathematical record and is explicitly excluded as a new special case; anisotropic affine transformations do not preserve this random-plane measure. No broader covering recorded result was identified in targeted searches. Historic Voss (1982) explicitly treats polygon-frequency formulas for unspecified polyhedron families, and Ohser–Mücklich (1995) treats regular-prism stereology; their full text was not available. These are material residual priority risks rather than evidence of a specific covering theorem. Independent historical validation remains necessary.

value.rationale: The section polygon-type distribution of a prism is a natural stereological observable. A complete formula for every right prism over a scalene triangle, with two distinct geometry-sensitive asymptotic coefficients, reveals how base shape is encoded at different aspect-ratio scales. The fact is substantially more informative than the known mean count and is not a mere normalization identity, arbitrary slice, or table recomputation.
